## Episode Thesis

Guest Maria Ljungqvist, a fixed-income manager at Aktieansvar, talks through rising long-term yields: the US 30-year is at its highest since 2007 and the Japanese 10-year at a 29-year high. She says the move is driven mainly by markets repricing Fed expectations toward rate hikes, together with Hormuz and energy-price inflation risk and tariff pass-through. She also covers Kevin Warsh taking over from Powell and the Riksbank, where the rates market prices a possible hike in September. Nordic high yield has returned just over 9% a year for three years. Tighter spreads mean future returns should be lower, but she still calls a roughly 6.5% yield before credit losses attractive, and says bond markets have re-rated Swedish real estate companies while equity markets have not.
